This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
On 06-10-2024 at about 04-30 pm., the petitioner was traveling in a Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ND-6489 as an occupant and when the said car was reached near Vijayapura- Jaipura Bridge, BM bypass road, Ramanagara Tq & District, at that time the driver of Bolero City Pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL- 5643 came in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly stopped his vehicle in the middle of the road,
due to that, the driver of the vehicle in which petitioner was traveling dashed to Bolero vehicle, result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Bharath Kempanna Hospital, Bidadi,
wherein admitted as an inpatient.
So far, the petitioner has spent more than Rs.4,00,000/- towards medicine, treatment nourishing and traveling expenses.

The doctor advised her orally to undergone one more surgery, the approximate cost of which is Rs.1,00,000/-.
2(a). Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
The petitioner was working as Analyst in Accenture and earning sum of Rs.32,000/- per month.
Due to the permanent disability, she is not in a position to do the said work.
She has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability, loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. Respondent no.2/

the insurer of Bolero City Pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 has filed written statement and contended that though two vehicles were involved in the alleged accident but the petitioner has not impleaded the driver of both the vehicles viz., Bolero city Pick up vehicle and Maruti Suzuku vehicle bearing No.KA-04-ND-6489 as party to the petition and that the driver of both the vehicles were not holding valid driving license.

The respondent no.2 further contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of Maruti Suzuki car and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Bolero City Pick up vehicle.

4. Respondent no.4/the insurer of Maruti Suzuki vehicle bearing No.KA-04-ND-6489 has filed written statement and contended that the driver of the Maruti Suzuki vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license and the said vehicle was not having valid permit and Fitness certificate and that the said Maruti Suzuki vehicle was proceeding in slow manner, by following all traffic rules and regulations, at that time the driver of Bolero Pickup vehicle drove the same in high speed,
without following traffic rules and stopped in the middle of the road without giving any signal and caused for the accident and that after investigation, the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of Bolero City Pick up vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643.
The respondent no.4 further contended that at the time of alleged accident petitioner was proceeding in the car without wearing seat belt in violation of Motor Vehicle Rules.
5. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 and 3 have remained absent.

Hence they were placed ex-parte.
6.

On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves

that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 06-10-2024 at about 4-30 p.m., near Vijayapura,
Jaipur Bridge, BM bypass road, Ramanagara Tq and District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Bolero city Pickup vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643

? 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

Issue No.1: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.

has relied upon Ex.P1 to 6 which are the police records such as FIR with complaint, Spot mahazar, sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, charge sheet, etc.,
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Shankarachari, case has been registered against the driver of Bolera Pickup Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 in Crime No.207/2024 by Ramanagara Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 106, 125(a), 281 of BNS 2023.

After completion of investigation, the Investigation officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable under Section 281, 125(a), 125(b), 106() of BNS 2023.
13.

It is true that based on the complaint lodged by the complainant against the driver of the offending vehicle, FIR was registered against him and after investigation charge sheet was filed against him.

The PW.1 during her cross examination by the learned counsel for respondent no.4 has Hemavathi M vs Praveen Kumar E on 5 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76182901/
4 deposed that the accident in question has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle who without giving any signal suddenly stopped the vehicle in the middle of the road and their vehicle was proceeding slowly and that she is not claiming compensation from the insurer and insured of the car bearing No.KA-04-MD-6489.

sentences.text: Even though the PW.1 in her evidence has deposed that she is not claiming compensation from the respondent no.3 and 4 and that the accident in question has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and even though complaint was lodged and charge sheet was filed only against the driver of the offending vehicle but if the claim petition filed by the complainant is perused, wherein she has stated that accident in question was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of both the vehicles and that respondents no.1 to 4 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

15. As per the evidence of the PW.1 her brother Chethan Kumar is the RC owner of the car in which she was traveling and on the fateful day of the accident her family members including her mother Gowramma were traveling in the said vehicle and due to the accident her mother succumbed to the injuries.
16. If the averments of the complaint, charge sheet and the claim petition is perused, at the time of accident the offending vehicle was proceeding ahead of Maruthi Car.
The width of the road at the spot of accident is nearly 60 feet.
The accident in question has occurred on the left side of the road.
It is one way road.
There is divider in between two roads leading from Bangalore to Mysore and Mysore to Bangalore.

When the width of the road is sufficiently wide to an extent of 60 feet and when accident in question has occurred on the left side of the road., there was sufficient road on the right side of the said road.

Hence, when offending vehicle was proceeding on the left side of the road, the driver of the Maruthi car which was proceeding behind the offending vehicle could have drive his vehicle on the right side of the road.

Further if the driver of the Maruthi car had maintained minimum distance between the two vehicles, even if the driver of the offending vehicle suddenly stopped the vehicle had without giving any signal, the driver of the Maruthi car could have avoided the accident.

Even though from the police records more particularly the complaint, spot mahazar, sketch and IMV report discloses the rash and negligent act contributed even by the driver of the Maruthi car but the investigating officer for the reason best known to him has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle.

It appears that it is because all the inmates of the Car have sustained injuries and one of the injured succumbed to the injuries, out of humanitarian ground to help the injured and family of the deceased the investigating officer might have filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle.
17. The officials of respondent no.2 and 4 company have adduced their evidence as RW.1 and RW.2 and given evidence blaming the driver of their opposite vehicle as the sole cause for the accident.
If the affidavit filed by the RW.1 is perused, wherein they have addressed the petitioner as "deceased".
In the evidence in chief of RW.1 they have stated that the driver of both the vehicles have contributed negligence.

sentences.text: The Learned counsel for respondent no.4 has relied upon the judgment reported in ILR 2016 KAR 55 between M/s ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd., Vs. Smt. Bharthi Reddy & Ors.,

entities.text: ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd., Vs. Smt. Bharthi Reddy & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the Tribunal has observed by relying upon the spot sketch that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The Hon'ble High Court held that "the Tribunal is justified in fastening liability on the Insurer and directed to indemnify the award.

The Hon'ble High Court further held that the charge sheet filed by the jurisdictional police is the conclusive proof and that same has not been questioned or challenged by the insurer.
19.
Coming to the case in hand, on perusal of the entire police records, it can be said that the driver of both the vehicles have equally contributed negligence.

Merely because the investigating officer has filed charge sheet only against the driver of the offending vehicle, the court cannot by relying upon the same hold that the driver of the offending vehicle alone has contributed negligence.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in catena of decisions time and again has observed that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof and the Tribunal has to independently decide the case based on the evidence placed on record.

In the judgment relied by the learned counsel for respondent no.4, it was proved from the spot sketch that the accident in question was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Hence, it was observed so.
But in the present case from the spot mahazar and from the IMV report it can be gathered that negligence was contributed by the driver of both the vehicles.
As per the spot sketch, after the accident Maruthi Suzuki Car has hit to the Iron fencing.
Further as per the IMV report much damage was caused to the Car.
From the aforesaid materials also it can be gathered the speed at which Maruthi Car was at the time of accident.

Hence,
considering the materials placed on record this court is of the opinion that the driver of the both vehicles have contributed negligence at the ratio of 50:50.
Hence, point no.1 is answered in Partly affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:- The petitioner has given evidence to the effect of her sustained grievous injuries.
As observed earlier, petitioner has produced medical documents i.e., Wound certificate and Discharge summary which are at Ex.P.5 and Ex.P7.
On going through the medical documents, it reveals that petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient from 06-10- 2024 to 10-10-2024 at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Ramanagara for a period of 5 days.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained three injuries which are grievous in nature.
21. The petitioner has not examined the medical officer who has given treatment to her and there is no evidence on record to say that petitioner has suffered permanent disability.
Further, petitioner has admitted that even after the accident she is receiving salary of Rs.32,000/- which she was receiving earlier to the accident.
As such there is no loss of future income.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income.
22. Towards pain and sufferings, the petitioner shown to have sustained three grievous injuries.

Hence taking into consideration the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, time taken for treatment and sufferings during the treatment etc, it is reasonable to hold that petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.70,000/- towards pain and suffering.

sentences.text: So far as the medical expenses incurred by the petitioner is concerned, she has produced 5 medical bills for Rs.6,850/- as per Ex.P8.

The petitioner has deposed that she has incurred medical expenses and other incidental expenses to the tune of Rs.4,00,000/- and medical expenses was reimbursed and towards un- cliamed medical bills she has claimed compensation under the head medical expenses.

When petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient for 5 days in private hospital definitely she would have incurred higher medical expenses and after reimbursement of medical expenses regarding left out medical bills, she has produced the same and claimed compensation of Rs.6,850/-.

Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.6,850/-.
24.
It is stated that petitioner was aged about 29 years.
She was working as Analyst in Accenture and drawing salary of Rs.32,000/- p.m..
But to substantiate the said contention petitioner has not produced any materials.

Hence this court considering the age of petitioner, year of accident and place of residence of the petitioner, taken the income of the petitioner at Rs.16,500/- p.m.
25.
The petitioner has sustained three grievous injuries and has taken treatment for 5 days as inpatient at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Ramanagara.
Hence the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, which are grievous in nature it is reasonable to hold that period of 2 months as complete laid down period.

Hence taking into consideration the avocation of petitioner and loss of income caused from the said avocation, this court takes the loss of income during laid down period as Rs.16,500/- p.m. for two month.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.33,000/-
towards loss of income during the laid down period .
26. From the evidence of Pw1 and as borne out by medical records, petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Bharath Kempanna Health Care, Ramanagara.
Further for taking treatment as inpatient in the said hospital she was traveled to hospital for treatment.
She has taken nourishment and needs further nourishment at this age and incurred other incidental expenses.
Therefore all together incidental expenses is assessed at Rs.25,000/- taking in to consideration the cost of living and value of the money during the year 2024.
27. The petitioner at her age of 29 years has suffered grievous injuries which definitely would cause some amount of discomfort and loss of amenities in life.
Hence, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head loss of amenities and discomfort to the tune of Rs.70,000/-.

Thus the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 Sl. Heads Amount  No.
 1. Towards pain and sufferings Rs. 70,000/-

2 . Medical expenses Rs. 6,850/-
 3. Loss of income during laid down Rs. 33,000  period  4. Towards Conveyance, Attendant Rs. 25,000/-
 charges and nourishing food  & other incidental charges

Therefore this court holds that petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,04,850/- (Rupees Two Lakh Four Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty only).
28.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

29. Hence, the respondent no.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN-12-AL-5643 is liable to pay compensation to an extent of 50% and remaining 50%
compensation shall be paid by the respondent no.4 being the insurer of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA-04-ND-6489.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total compensation of 2,04,850/- + cost of Rs.2,000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I & II.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.2,06,850/- (Rupees Two Lakh Six Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty only).
A Sum of Rs.2,04,850/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Respondent No 2 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.1,02,425/- +
cost of Rs.2000/- imposed vide order on IA No.I and II.

The respondent no.2 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.1,04,425/- (Rupees One Lakh Four Thousand Four Hundred Twenty Five only) with interest at 6% within 2 months from the date of this award.
The Respondent No 4 is liable to pay 50% of the compensation amount i.e., sum of Rs.1,02,425/-.
The respondent no.4 is directed to deposit the compensation of Rs.1,02,425/- (Rupees One Lakh Two Thousand Four Hundred Twenty Five only) along with interest within two months from the date of award.
On deposit entire amount and interest is ordered to be released in favour of the petitioner on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
